title: A Well for the Harvest
premise: Late-night radio host Casper Vasquez has built a career on skepticism, so when callers begin phoning in — people he can verify died the previous week — he assumes a hoax, then a breakdown, then something worse. The calls all trace to Hollow Creek Farm, where an excavation crew has just broken open a door sealed from the inside a century ago, and every voice on his line belongs to someone the farm took before. As the crew — foreman Delia Marsh, her estranged brother Tomas, and archaeologist Ruth Okafor — barricade themselves against what they invited in, Casper realizes the dead aren't haunting them; they're warning him, because his own family name is on the original invitation. To end it, Casper must drive to the farm before sunrise and answer the door as his bloodline always should have, choosing love for the living over the duty of inheritance that has fed the thing below for four generations.
about_author: Gideon Winterbourne is the pen name of a former rural radio engineer who spent fifteen years maintaining transmitter towers across the American heartland and collecting the stories nobody would say on air. A Well for the Harvest is their third novel, following two critically ignored books about small towns that refuse to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Dead Air Hour
chapters.summary: Casper Vasquez hosts 'Open Line' from a dying AM station, mocking supernatural callers with practiced cruelty. At 2:13 a.m., a woman phones in describing her own funeral from last Tuesday. POV: Casper. Beat: unease disguised as professional amusement.

chapters.title: Verification
chapters.summary: Casper checks the obituary; Marlene Duffy died six days ago. He assumes an elaborate prank by his rival station and plays along on air, but the caller knows things only Marlene knew. POV: Casper. Beat: the first crack in certainty.

chapters.title: Hollow Creek Breaks Ground
chapters.summary: Delia Marsh's excavation crew begins work on the old Vasquez family farmland, contracted to clear it for development. Her crew chief complains the soil is wrong — too soft, too warm. POV: Delia. Beat: quiet dread beneath routine labor.

chapters.title: Second Caller
chapters.summary: A man calls claiming to be Reverend Amos Pell, dead since 1924, and recites the exact words of a document Casper has never seen. The call drops when Casper asks about his grandmother. POV: Casper. Beat: personal stakes surface.

chapters.title: The Door
chapters.summary: The crew unearths a stone doorway set flush into the earth, its iron ring fused shut — sealed, Ruth confirms, from the inside. Delia orders photos and a halt, but the developer pressures them onward. POV: Delia. Beat: discovery and denial.

chapters.title: Ruth's Notes
chapters.summary: Archaeologist Ruth Okafor finds 1890s records: the farm's well ran dry the same week the door was sealed, and eleven people vanished over forty years. She keeps this from the crew. POV: Ruth. Beat: guilt of withheld knowledge.

chapters.title: The Voice on the Tape
chapters.summary: Casper plays back the night's calls; between words, a second voice breathes his childhood nickname no one alive uses. His producer hears nothing. POV: Casper. Beat: isolation of the witness.

chapters.title: Tomas Opens It
chapters.summary: Drunk and furious at his sister, Tomas pries the ring loose. The door swings inward into darkness that doesn't echo. That night, crew member Sal walks toward the field and doesn't come back. POV: Tomas. Beat: transgression and first loss.

chapters.title: Sal Calls In
chapters.summary: Sal phones the radio show, calm, describing standing in a harvest that never ends. He asks Casper to tell his wife the door was already open when he got there. POV: Casper. Beat: grief transmitted through disbelief.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Delia pulls the crew into the farmhouse, boards windows, counts heads: five remain. Phones work inward only. Something circles the yard, patient, unhurried. POV: Delia. Beat: siege mentality forms.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Ruth deciphers the deed: the land was granted to a Vasquez ancestor under covenant — 'a well for the harvest' — a tithe of lives owed each generation. The seal was maintenance, not protection. POV: Ruth. Beat: horror reframed as contract law.

chapters.title: Family Business
chapters.summary: Casper researches his surname and finds his great-grandfather signed the covenant; every heir since has paid or fled. His father's suicide note suddenly reads differently. POV: Casper. Beat: inheritance becomes indictment.

chapters.title: What the Corn Remembers
chapters.summary: The dead callers begin coaching Casper — Marlene explains the rules, Amos warns what breaks them. They were invited too, once, and want the line ended. POV: Casper. Beat: the dead become allies.

chapters.title: First Breach
chapters.summary: Something wears Sal's voice at the farmhouse door, asking to be let in from the cold. Crew member Imani nearly opens it; Delia stops her with a crowbar through the frame. POV: Delia. Beat: loyalty tested against mercy.

chapters.title: Imani's Bargain
chapters.summary: Exhausted, Imani confesses she heard the thing promise her son's illness cured if she opened up. The group fractures over whether she's traitor or victim. POV: Ruth. Beat: compassion versus survival.

chapters.title: The Well
chapters.summary: Tomas investigates the dry wellhouse and finds it descends past any plausible depth, walls carved with names — the newest still wet. His own is half-finished. POV: Tomas. Beat: doom made literal and personal.

chapters.title: Sunrise Lie
chapters.summary: Dawn comes and nothing stops; the sun rises gray and distant, like light through water. Ruth realizes time outside the farm runs differently now. POV: Delia. Beat: the rules have changed.

chapters.title: Call From the Inside
chapters.summary: Casper receives a call from the farmhouse landline — a number that shouldn't connect. It's Delia, and hearing a live voice breaks something open in him: these are real people. POV: Casper. Beat: skeptic chooses to believe.

chapters.title: The Drive Out
chapters.summary: Casper abandons the studio mid-broadcast, leaving the mic open so the dead can keep talking to whoever listens. He drives toward Hollow Creek as the sky refuses to brighten. POV: Casper. Beat: commitment.

chapters.title: Roadblock
chapters.summary: The highway loops back on itself three times. The dead coach him through: the road obeys the covenant, and only a Vasquez walking the last mile will find the gate. POV: Casper. Beat: the trap narrows by design.

chapters.title: Imani Goes Out
chapters.summary: Desperate for her son, Iani slips out at dusk. Through the window they watch the field take her gently, almost kindly — which is worse. POV: Delia. Beat: hope weaponized.

chapters.title: Brother, Sister
chapters.summary: Tomas breaks down; he opened the door to spite Delia, who got the farm in the will while he got nothing. Their fight becomes confession, then forgiveness. POV: Tomas. Beat: love against resentment.

chapters.title: The Original Terms
chapters.summary: Ruth translates the full covenant: the heir may refuse the inheritance, but refusal requires answering the door in person and naming what they love more than the land. No heir has managed it. POV: Ruth. Beat: the mechanism of escape revealed.

chapters.title: Static Choir
chapters.summary: At the station, the open mic fills with hundreds of voices singing the harvest hymn — listeners worldwide call in terrified, hearing their own relatives among the choir. POV: Casper (via broadcast). Beat: scale widens; the story leaks out.

chapters.title: Arrival
chapters.summary: Casper reaches the fence line on foot as instructed. The farmhouse lights burn warm and welcoming, exactly like home. Delia watches him cross the yard through a rifle scope, unsure if he's rescue or bait. POV: Delia. Beat: wary convergence.

chapters.title: Quarantine Argument
chapters.summary: Inside, the group debates using Casper as the tithe — he's the heir, after all. Delia refuses; Ruth argues the covenant demands willingness, not sacrifice. Casper agrees to try. POV: Casper. Beat: moral fault lines drawn.

chapters.title: The Door Answers
chapters.summary: Before dawn rehearsal, the door knocks first. It speaks in Casper's father's voice, offering absolution, offering rest. Tomas nearly answers; the dead scream through the radios to stop him. POV: Tomas. Beat: temptation peaks.

chapters.title: Preparations
chapters.summary: They fortify, inventory, and say the unsaid things. Delia gives Casper her father's watch — 'so you know how long forever takes.' Quiet chapter of humanity before the storm. POV: Delia. Beat: tenderness under pressure.

chapters.title: The Long Night Begins
chapters.summary: Sunset comes early and wrong. The house groans as the ground shifts; the well begins to sing. Every window shows the cornfield closer than it was. POV: Ruth. Beat: dread crescendo.

chapters.title: Breach
chapters.summary: The walls fail. The thing enters wearing everyone they've lost at once — Sal, Imani, Marlene, Amos — each pleading their case. The survivors cling together in the cellar as the house dissolves above. POV: Delia. Beat: overwhelming assault.

chapters.title: Cellar Descent
chapters.summary: Chased downward, they discover the cellar connects to the well shaft. The only way out is through: down past the carved names to the door itself. POV: Tomas. Beat: retreat becomes advance.

chapters.title: The Names
chapters.summary: Descending, they read the wall — generations of Vasquezes, and at the bottom, fresh-cut: CASPER. He touches it and feels the thing reading him back. POV: Casper. Beat: identity as battleground.

chapters.title: Father's Voice
chapters.summary: In the dark, the thing drops its masks and speaks plainly: it is tired, it is hungry, it only ever wanted to be released by consent. Casper almost pities it. POV: Casper. Beat: horror gains tragic dimension.

chapters.title: Delia's Stand
chapters.summary: The thing offers Delia the farm free and clear, Tomas restored, if she hands over Casper. She answers with the crowbar and buys minutes with blood. POV: Delia. Beat: love against duty, embodied.

chapters.title: Answering the Door
chapters.summary: Casper reaches the inner door and opens it from the inside — reversing the original seal. What waits isn't a monster but a vast, starving patience older than the deed. He must speak now or be spoken for. POV: Casper. Beat: threshold moment.

chapters.title: What He Loves More
chapters.summary: Casper renounces the inheritance aloud — not the land, but the silence, the lies, the dead kept as currency — and names the living: the strangers in the cellar, the listeners on the line, even the thing itself, offered pity instead of fear. The covenant has no clause for mercy. POV: Casper. Beat: climax; love as legal loophole.

chapters.title: Collapse
chapters.summary: The covenant breaks. The well floods upward with everything it took, returning the dead for one minute of goodbye — Sal to his wife via the phone, Imani's voice to the wind — then the farm folds into ordinary dirt. POV: Ruth. Beat: catharsis and cost.

chapters.title: Sunrise, Actually
chapters.summary: True dawn. Four survivors walk out of a featureless field onto a highway where traffic moves normally. Delia's watch stopped at the hour of the breach and starts again. POV: Delia. Beat: release.

chapters.title: Sign-Off
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Casper returns to the air, changed — gentler with callers, haunted but whole. His final caller says thank you and hangs up before he can ask her name. Some debts, he decides, stay paid quietly. POV: Casper. Beat: bittersweet resolution.

chapters.title: Epilogue: Soil Report
chapters.summary: Ruth publishes nothing; some doors should stay scholarly rumor. But at the filled-in wellhead, someone has planted corn — one row, thriving, facing the house. And on windless nights, it leans toward the road, listening for cars. POV: omniscient. Beat: the last cold shiver.
